sanskrit: vaiyāghrakośas tu mahān bhīmasenasya sāyakaḥ gurubhārasaho divyaḥ śātravāṇāṃ bhayaṃkaraḥ
english: The great tiger-skin-scabbarded sword belonging to Bhīmasena — divine, capable of bearing heavy weight — is a source of terror to his enemies.

sanskrit: suphalaś citrakośaś ca hematsarur anuttamaḥ nistriṃśaḥ kauravasyaiṣa dharmarājasya dhīmataḥ
english: This straight-bladed sword with a beautiful variegated scabbard and a golden hilt, unsurpassed in excellence, belongs to the Kaurava Dharmarāja, the wise one.

sanskrit: yas tu pāñcanakhe kośe nihitaś citrasevane nakulasyaiṣa nistriṃśo gurubhārasaho dṛḍhaḥ
english: This straight-bladed sword stored in a scabbard adorned with five-nailed designs and bright embellishments — heavy-bearing and firm — belongs to Nakula.

sanskrit: yas tv ayaṃ vimalaḥ khaḍgo gavye kośe samarpitaḥ sahadevasya viddhy enaṃ sarvabhārasahaṃ dṛḍham
english: Know that this spotless sword sheathed in a cowhide scabbard, capable of bearing all weight and firm, belongs to Sahadeva.

sanskrit: uttara uvāca suvarṇavikṛtānīmāny āyudhāni mahātmanām rucirāṇi prakāśante pārthānām āśukāriṇām
english: Uttara said: These weapons of the great-souled Pārthas, wrought with gold and variously fashioned, shine beautifully — belonging to swift-acting warriors.

sanskrit: kva nu svid arjunaḥ pārthaḥ kauravyo vā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca bhīmasenaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Where indeed are Arjuna the son of Pṛthā, or the Kaurava Yudhiṣṭhira, and Nakula and Sahadeva and Bhīmasena the Pāṇḍava?

sanskrit: sarva eva mahātmānaḥ sarvāmitravināśanāḥ rājyam akṣaiḥ parākīrya na śrūyante kadā cana
english: All of them — great souls, destroyers of all enemies — having lost their kingdom at dice, are never heard of anymore.

sanskrit: draupadī kva ca pāñcālī strīratnam iti viśrutā jitān akṣais tadā kṛṣṇā tān evānvagamad vanam
english: And where is Draupadī the Pāñcālī, celebrated as a jewel among women? When the dark one's husbands were defeated at dice, she followed them into the forest.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca aham asmy arjunaḥ pārthaḥ sabhāstāro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ ballavo bhīmasenas tu pitus te rasapācakaḥ
english: Arjuna said: I am Arjuna, son of Pṛthā. Yudhiṣṭhira is the keeper of the assembly hall. Bhīmasena is Ballava, your father's cook.

sanskrit: aśvabandho 'tha nakulaḥ sahadevas tu gokule sairandhrīṃ draupadīṃ viddhi yatkṛte kīcakā hatāḥ
english: Nakula is the horse-keeper, and Sahadeva works among the cattle. Know Draupadī to be the Sairandhrī on whose account Kīcaka was slain.

sanskrit: uttara uvāca daśa pārthasya nāmāni yāni pūrvaṃ śrutāni me prabrūyās tāni yadi me śraddadhyāṃ sarvam eva te
english: Uttara said: If you were to recite for me the ten names of the son of Pṛthā that I have heard before, then I would believe everything you say.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca hanta te 'haṃ samācakṣe daśa nāmāni yāni me arjunaḥ phalguno jiṣṇuḥ kirīṭī śvetavāhanaḥ bībhatsur vijayaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ savyasācī dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Arjuna said: Come then, I shall tell you my ten names: Arjuna, Phalguna, Jiṣṇu, Kiriti, Shvetavahana, Bībhatsu, Vijaya, Kṛṣṇa, Savyasācin, and Dhanañjaya.

sanskrit: uttara uvāca kenāsi vijayo nāma kenāsi śvetavāhanaḥ kirīṭī nāma kenāsi savyasācī kathaṃ bhavān
english: Uttara said: Why are you called Vijaya? Why are you called Shvetavahana? Why Kiriti? And how are you Savyasācin?

sanskrit: arjunaḥ phalguno jiṣṇuḥ kṛṣṇo bībhatsur eva ca dhanaṃjayaś ca kenāsi prabrūhi mama tattvataḥ śrutā me tasya vīrasya kevalā nāmahetavaḥ
english: And why are you Arjuna, Phalguna, Jiṣṇu, Kṛṣṇa, Bībhatsu, and Dhanañjaya? Tell me truly. I have heard only the names of that hero, but not the reasons for them.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca sarvāñ janapadāñ jitvā vittam ācchidya kevalam madhye dhanasya tiṣṭhāmi tenāhur māṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: Arjuna said: Having conquered all the realms and seized their wealth alone, I stand at the center of that treasure — therefore they call me Dhanañjaya, the winner of wealth.

sanskrit: abhiprayāmi saṃgrāme yad ahaṃ yuddhadurmadān nājitvā vinivartāmi tena māṃ vijayaṃ viduḥ
english: Because when I advance into battle against those arrogant in war, I do not turn back without conquering — therefore they know me as Vijaya, the victorious.

sanskrit: śvetāḥ kāñcanasaṃnāhā rathe yujyanti me hayāḥ saṃgrāme yudhyamānasya tenāhaṃ śvetavāhanaḥ
english: White horses clad in golden armor are yoked to my chariot when I fight in battle — therefore I am Shvetavahana, the one with white steeds.

sanskrit: uttarābhyāṃ ca pūrvābhyāṃ phalgunībhyām ahaṃ divā jāto himavataḥ pṛṣṭhe tena māṃ phalgunaṃ viduḥ
english: I was born by day on the slopes of the Himālayas under the two Phālgunī asterisms — northern and southern — therefore they know me as Phalguna.

sanskrit: purā śakreṇa me dattaṃ yudhyato dānavarṣabhaiḥ kirīṭaṃ mūrdhni sūryābhaṃ tena māhuḥ kirīṭinam
english: Long ago Śakra gave me, while I was fighting the lords of the Dānavas, a diadem radiant as the sun placed on my head — therefore they call me Kiriti, the diademed one.

sanskrit: na kuryāṃ karma bībhatsaṃ yudhyamānaḥ kathaṃ cana tena devamanuṣyeṣu bībhatsur iti māṃ viduḥ
english: I would never perform a loathsome deed in any manner while fighting — therefore among gods and men they know me as Bībhatsu, the one who shuns the abhorrent.

sanskrit: ubhau me dakṣiṇau pāṇī gāṇḍīvasya vikarṣaṇe tena devamanuṣyeṣu savyasācīti māṃ viduḥ
english: Both my hands are right-handed in the drawing of the Gāṇḍīva bow — therefore among gods and men they call me Savyasācin, the ambidextrous.

sanskrit: pṛthivyāṃ caturantāyāṃ varṇo me durlabhaḥ samaḥ karomi karma śuklaṃ ca tena mām arjunaṃ viduḥ
english: In the earth bounded by its four limits, my hue is rare and unblemished, and I perform pure deeds — therefore they know me as Arjuna, the bright one.

sanskrit: ahaṃ durāpo durdharṣo damanaḥ pākaśāsaniḥ tena devamanuṣyeṣu jiṣṇunāmāsmi viśrutaḥ
english: I am hard to approach, difficult to assail, a tamer of foes, the chastiser of Pāka — therefore among gods and men I am renowned by the name Jiṣṇu, the triumphant.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇa ity eva daśamaṃ nāma cakre pitā mama kṛṣṇāvadātasya sataḥ priyatvād bālakasya vai
english: My father gave me Kṛṣṇa as my tenth name out of affection for the child, me, who was dark yet spotless and virtuous.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ pārthaṃ sa vairāṭir abhyavādayad antikāt ahaṃ bhūmiṃjayo nāma nāmnāham api cottaraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the son of Virāṭa approached the son of Pṛthā and greeted him respectfully, saying: "My name is Bhuminjaya, and I am also called Uttara."

sanskrit: diṣṭyā tvāṃ pārtha paśyāmi svāgataṃ te dhanaṃjaya lohitākṣa mahābāho nāgarājakaropama yad ajñānād avocaṃ tvāṃ kṣantum arhasi tan mama
english: "By good fortune do I behold you, O Pārtha! Welcome, O Dhanañjaya, red-eyed and mighty-armed, like the hood of a lord of serpents! Whatever I said to you in ignorance, please forgive me for that."

sanskrit: yatas tvayā kṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ vicitraṃ karma duṣkaram ato bhayaṃ vyatītaṃ me prītiś ca paramā tvayi
english: "Because of the wondrous and difficult deeds you have performed in the past, my fear has passed away and my affection for you is the greatest."

sanskrit: uttara uvāca āsthāya vipulaṃ vīra rathaṃ sārathinā mayā katamaṃ yāsyase 'nīkam ukto yāsyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: Uttara said: Having mounted your great chariot, O hero, with me as charioteer, against which army will you advance? Tell me, and I shall go there as you direct.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca prīto 'smi puruṣavyāghra na bhayaṃ vidyate tava sarvān nudāmi te śatrūn raṇe raṇaviśārada
english: Arjuna said: I am pleased, O tiger among men! There is no fear for you. I shall drive away all your enemies in battle, O you who are skilled in combat.

sanskrit: svastho bhava mahābuddhe paśya māṃ śatrubhiḥ saha yudhyamānaṃ vimarde 'smin kurvāṇaṃ bhairavaṃ mahat
english: Be at ease, O great-minded one! Watch me fighting with the enemies in this clash, performing a great and terrifying feat.

sanskrit: etān sarvān upāsaṅgān kṣipraṃ badhnīhi me rathe etaṃ cāhara nistriṃśaṃ jātarūpapariṣkṛtam ahaṃ vai kurubhir yotsyāmy avajeṣyāmi te paśūn
english: Quickly fasten all these quivers to my chariot, and bring that straight-bladed sword adorned with pure gold — I shall indeed fight the Kurus and win back your cattle.

sanskrit: saṃkalpapakṣavikṣepaṃ bāhuprākāratoraṇam tridaṇḍatūṇasaṃbādham anekadhvajasaṃkulam
english: With wings spread by intent, its archways formed by mighty arms, thronged with triple-staffed quivers and crowded with many banners —

sanskrit: jyākṣepaṇaṃ krodhakṛtaṃ nemīninadadundubhi nagaraṃ te mayā guptaṃ rathopasthaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: — with the twanging of the bowstring done in wrath, the rumble of the wheel-rims like a kettledrum, this chariot beneath you shall be, for you, a city protected by me.

sanskrit: adhiṣṭhito mayā saṃkhye ratho gāṇḍīvadhanvanā ajeyaḥ śatrusainyānāṃ vairāṭe vyetu te bhayam
english: This chariot, commanded in battle by me, the bearer of the Gāṇḍīva bow, is unconquerable by enemy armies, O son of Virāṭa! Let your fear depart.

sanskrit: uttara uvāca bibhemi nāham eteṣāṃ jānāmi tvāṃ sthiraṃ yudhi keśavenāpi saṃgrāme sākṣād indreṇa vā samam
english: Uttara said: I do not fear them; I know you to be steadfast in battle, equal in combat even to Keśava himself, or indeed to Indra in person.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu cintayann eva parimuhyāmi kevalam niścayaṃ cāpi durmedhā na gacchāmi kathaṃ cana
english: Yet pondering this very thing I become utterly confused — being of poor understanding, I cannot in any way reach a conclusion.

sanskrit: evaṃ vīrāṅgarūpasya lakṣaṇair ucitasya ca kena karmavipākena klībatvam idam āgatam
english: For one whose body is that of a hero and who is endowed with appropriate marks of distinction — how has this state of being a eunuch come about through the ripening of deeds?

sanskrit: manye tvāṃ klībaveṣeṇa carantaṃ śūlapāṇinam gandharvarājapratimaṃ devaṃ vāpi śatakratum
english: I think you to be the trident-bearing god himself, or perhaps the king of the Gandharvas, moving about in the disguise of a eunuch — or even Śatakratu, the god of a hundred sacrifices.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca bhrātur niyogāj jyeṣṭhasya saṃvatsaram idaṃ vratam carāmi brahmacaryaṃ vai satyam etad bravīmi te
english: Arjuna said: By the command of my eldest brother I have observed this vow for a year, practicing celibacy — this is the truth I tell you.

sanskrit: nāsmi klībo mahābāho paravān dharmasaṃyutaḥ samāptavratam uttīrṇaṃ viddhi māṃ tvaṃ nṛpātmaja
english: I am not a eunuch, O mighty-armed one — I am bound by dharma, subject to another's will. Know me to have completed my vow and to have passed through it, O son of a king.

sanskrit: uttara uvāca paramo 'nugraho me 'dya yat pratarko na me vṛthā na hīdṛśāḥ klībarūpā bhavantīha narottamāḥ
english: Uttara said: Today I receive the greatest favor, because my inference was not in vain — for those of eunuch appearance are surely not supreme men of this kind.

sanskrit: sahāyavān asmi raṇe yudhyeyam amarair api sādhvasaṃ tat pranaṣṭaṃ me kiṃ karomi bravīhi me
english: I shall be your ally in battle and could fight even against the immortals! My timidity has vanished. Tell me — what shall I do?

sanskrit: ahaṃ te saṃgrahīṣyāmi hayāñ śatrurathārujaḥ śikṣito hy asmi sārathye tīrthataḥ puruṣarṣabha
english: I shall hold the reins of your horses, breaker of enemy chariots — for I am trained in chariot-driving through proper instruction, O bull among men.

sanskrit: dāruko vāsudevasya yathā śakrasya mātaliḥ tathā māṃ viddhi sārathye śikṣitaṃ narapuṃgava
english: As Dāruka is to Vāsudeva, as Matali is to Śakra, so know me to be trained in chariotship, O foremost of men.

sanskrit: yasya yāte na paśyanti bhūmau prāptaṃ padaṃ padam dakṣiṇaṃ yo dhuraṃ yuktaḥ sugrīvasadṛśo hayaḥ
english: The horse yoked on the right shaft, resembling Sugrīva in quality, is one whose hoof-prints on the ground cannot be seen as he gallops.

sanskrit: yo 'yaṃ dhuraṃ dhuryavaro vāmaṃ vahati śobhanaḥ taṃ manye meghapuṣpasya javena sadṛśaṃ hayam
english: This splendid horse, best of draft animals, who draws the left shaft — I consider it equal in speed to Meghapuṣpa.

sanskrit: yo 'yaṃ kāñcanasaṃnāhaḥ pārṣṇiṃ vahati śobhanaḥ vāmaṃ sainyasya manye taṃ javena balavattaram
english: This splendid horse clad in golden armor who draws the left flank-position — I consider it mightier in speed than the whole army's left flank.

sanskrit: yo 'yaṃ vahati te pārṣṇiṃ dakṣiṇām añcitodyataḥ balāhakād api mataḥ sa jave vīryavattaraḥ
english: This one who draws your right flank with body arched and neck raised — even compared to Balāhaka he is reckoned mightier in speed and valor.

sanskrit: tvām evāyaṃ ratho voḍhuṃ saṃgrāme 'rhati dhanvinam tvaṃ cemaṃ ratham āsthāya yoddhum arho mato mama
english: This chariot is worthy of carrying you, the bowman, into battle; and you, having mounted this chariot, are worthy to fight — in my opinion.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato nirmucya bāhubhyāṃ valayāni sa vīryavān citre dundubhisaṃnāde pratyamuñcat tale śubhe
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then that valiant one removed the bracelets from his arms and, amid a wondrous kettledrum roll, slapped his two auspicious palms.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇān bhaṅgīmataḥ keśāñ śvetenodgrathya vāsasā adhijyaṃ tarasā kṛtvā gāṇḍīvaṃ vyākṣipad dhanuḥ
english: Having bound up his curly dark hair with a white cloth, he swiftly strung the Gāṇḍīva bow and bent it with force.

sanskrit: tasya vikṣipyamāṇasya dhanuṣo 'bhūn mahāsvanaḥ yathā śailasya mahataḥ śailenaivābhijaghnuṣaḥ
english: As that bow was being drawn, a great sound arose — like a great mountain being struck by another mountain.

sanskrit: sanirghātābhavad bhūmir dikṣu vāyur vavau bhṛśam bhrāntadvijaṃ khaṃ tadāsīt prakampitamahādrumam
english: The earth shook with thunderclaps; the wind blew mightily in all directions; the sky was filled with wheeling birds, and the great trees trembled.

sanskrit: taṃ śabdaṃ kuravo 'jānan visphoṭam aśaner iva yad arjuno dhanuḥśreṣṭhaṃ bāhubhyām ākṣipad rathe
english: The Kurus recognized that sound — like the cracking of a thunderbolt — as Arjuna drawing the foremost of bows with his arms upon the chariot.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca uttaraṃ sārathiṃ kṛtvā śamīṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam āyudhaṃ sarvam ādāya tataḥ prāyād dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having made Uttara his charioteer, having circumambulated the shami tree clockwise, and having taken up all the weapons, Dhanañjaya then set forth.

sanskrit: dhvajaṃ siṃhaṃ rathāt tasmād apanīya mahārathaḥ praṇidhāya śamīmūle prāyād uttarasārathiḥ
english: The great chariot-warrior removed the lion banner from that chariot, placed it at the root of the shami tree, and then departed with Uttara as his charioteer.

sanskrit: daivīṃ māyāṃ rathe yuktvā vihitāṃ viśvakarmaṇā kāñcanaṃ siṃhalāṅgūlaṃ dhvajaṃ vānaralakṣaṇam
english: Having attached to the chariot the divine magical device fashioned by Viśvakarman — the golden banner bearing a lion's tail and marked with a monkey —

sanskrit: manasā cintayām āsa prasādaṃ pāvakasya ca sa ca tac cintitaṃ jñātvā dhvaje bhūtāny acodayat
english: — he mentally meditated on and invoked the grace of Pāvaka (Fire); and Pāvaka, knowing what had been thought, impelled supernatural beings onto the banner.

sanskrit: sapatākaṃ vicitrāṅgaṃ sopāsaṅgaṃ mahārathaḥ ratham āsthāya bībhatsuḥ kaunteyaḥ śvetavāhanaḥ
english: Mounting the chariot adorned with banners and variously decorated limbs, with quivers attached, the great chariot-warrior Bībhatsu, son of Kuntī, the White-horsed one —

sanskrit: baddhāsiḥ satanutrāṇaḥ pragṛhītaśarāsanaḥ tataḥ prāyād udīcīṃ sa kapipravaraketanaḥ
english: — with sword girt on, clad in armor, and bow taken up in hand, he then marched northward, he who bears the banner of the foremost of monkeys.

sanskrit: svanavantaṃ mahāśaṅkhaṃ balavān arimardanaḥ prādhamad balam āsthāya dviṣatāṃ lomaharṣaṇam
english: The mighty crusher of enemies blew his great resonant conch with full strength — a sound that made the hair of his foes stand on end.

sanskrit: tatas te javanā dhuryā jānubhyām agaman mahīm uttaraś cāpi saṃtrasto rathopastha upāviśat
english: Then those swift draft horses fell to their knees upon the ground, and Uttara too, terror-stricken, sank down onto the chariot floor.

sanskrit: saṃsthāpya cāśvān kaunteyaḥ samudyamya ca raśmibhiḥ uttaraṃ ca pariṣvajya samāśvāsayad arjunaḥ
english: The son of Kuntī steadied the horses and raised them up with the reins; then Arjuna embraced Uttara and reassured him.

sanskrit: mā bhais tvaṃ rājaputrāgrya kṣatriyo 'si paraṃtapa kathaṃ puruṣaśārdūla śatrumadhye viṣīdasi
english: "Do not be afraid, O foremost of princes! You are a Kṣatriya, a scorcher of foes. How is it, O tiger among men, that you despond in the midst of enemies?"

sanskrit: śrutās te śaṅkhaśabdāś ca bherīśabdāś ca puṣkalāḥ kuñjarāṇāṃ ca nadatāṃ vyūḍhānīkeṣu tiṣṭhatām
english: "You have heard the sounds of conches and the full-toned sounds of war-drums, and the roaring of elephants standing in battle array —"

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ katham ihānena śaṅkhaśabdena bhīṣitaḥ viṣaṇṇarūpo vitrastaḥ puruṣaḥ prākṛto yathā
english: "— how is it that you, that very man, are now terrified by this conch-sound and appear dejected and frightened like an ordinary person?"

sanskrit: uttara uvāca śrutā me śaṅkhaśabdāś ca bherīśabdāś ca puṣkalāḥ kuñjarāṇāṃ ca ninadā vyūḍhānīkeṣu tiṣṭhatām
english: Uttara said: I have indeed heard the sounds of conches and the full-toned sounds of war-drums, and the cries of elephants standing in battle formations —

sanskrit: naivaṃvidhaḥ śaṅkhaśabdaḥ purā jātu mayā śrutaḥ dhvajasya cāpi rūpaṃ me dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ na hīdṛśam dhanuṣaś caiva nirghoṣaḥ śrutapūrvo na me kva cit
english: — but never before have I heard a conch-sound like this; nor have I ever seen a banner such as this before; nor anywhere have I ever heard the twang of a bow like this.

sanskrit: asya śaṅkhasya śabdena dhanuṣo nisvanena ca rathasya ca ninādena mano muhyati me bhṛśam
english: By the sound of this conch, by the twang of this bow, and by the rumbling of this chariot, my mind is utterly bewildered.

sanskrit: vyākulāś ca diśaḥ sarvā hṛdayaṃ vyathatīva me dhvajena pihitāḥ sarvā diśo na pratibhānti me gāṇḍīvasya ca śabdena karṇau me badhirīkṛtau
english: All the directions are turbulent and my heart seems to tremble; all directions appear concealed to me by that banner; and by the sound of the Gāṇḍīva my ears are deafened.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca ekānte ratham āsthāya padbhyāṃ tvam avapīḍaya dṛḍhaṃ ca raśmīn saṃyaccha śaṅkhaṃ dhmāsyāmy ahaṃ punaḥ
english: Arjuna said: Standing the chariot in a secluded spot, press down firmly with your feet and hold the reins tight — I shall blow the conch again.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasya śaṅkhasya śabdena rathanemisvanena ca gāṇḍīvasya ca ghoṣeṇa pṛthivī samakampata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: At the sound of that conch, the rumble of the chariot wheel-rims, and the roar of the Gāṇḍīva, the earth trembled.

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca yathā rathasya nirghoṣo yathā śaṅkha udīryate kampate ca yathā bhūmir naiṣo 'nyaḥ savyasācinaḥ
english: Droṇa said: The way this chariot resounds, the way this conch is blown, the way the earth trembles — this can be none other than Savyasācin.

sanskrit: śastrāṇi na prakāśante na prahṛṣyanti vājinaḥ agnayaś ca na bhāsante samiddhās tan na śobhanam
english: Our weapons do not shine; the horses do not grow spirited; and the fires do not blaze even when kindled — this is not auspicious.

sanskrit: praty ādityaṃ ca naḥ sarve mṛgā ghorapravādinaḥ dhvajeṣu ca nilīyante vāyasās tan na śobhanam śakunāś cāpasavyā no vedayanti mahad bhayam
english: All our animals cry ominously facing the sun; crows settle on the banners — that is not auspicious; and birds circle us inauspiciously on the left, presaging great danger.

sanskrit: gomāyur eṣa senāyā ruvan madhye 'nudhāvati anāhataś ca niṣkrānto mahad vedayate bhayam bhavatāṃ romakūpāṇi prahṛṣṭāny upalakṣaye
english: This jackal is howling and running through the middle of the army; it has come forth of itself without being struck and portends great danger; I observe that the hair on your bodies stands erect.

sanskrit: parābhūtā ca vaḥ senā na kaś cid yoddhum icchati vivarṇamukhabhūyiṣṭhāḥ sarve yodhā vicetasaḥ gāḥ saṃprasthāpya tiṣṭhāmo vyūḍhānīkāḥ prahāriṇaḥ
english: Your army is already defeated and no one wishes to fight; most of the warriors are pale-faced and bewildered. Let us drive away the cattle and stand here in battle array, ready to strike.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca atha duryodhano rājā samare bhīṣmam abravīt droṇaṃ ca rathaśārdūlaṃ kṛpaṃ ca sumahāratham
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then King Duryodhana spoke in the battle to Bhīṣma, and to Droṇa the tiger among chariot-warriors, and to Kṛpa the great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: ukto 'yam artha ācāryo mayā karṇena cāsakṛt punar eva ca vakṣyāmi na hi tṛpyāmi taṃ bruvan
english: "This matter has been spoken of by me and by Karṇa to the preceptor many times, and I shall say it again — for I am not satisfied merely speaking of it."

sanskrit: parājitair hi vastavyaṃ taiś ca dvādaśa vatsarān vane janapade 'jñātair eṣa eva paṇo hi naḥ
english: "The defeated ones must dwell — those defeated ones — for twelve years in the forest and a thirteenth year unrecognized among people; this indeed was the stake agreed upon by us."
